sources.title: Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala, El primer nueva corónica y buen gobierno (manuscript c. 1615/1616), Royal Danish Library digital edition.

verification.note: Indexed Royal Library edition heading and contents checked: autograph manuscript dated 1615/1616, Andean and colonial historical sections and dialogue with the king. Direct opening returned 403. Bibliographic inclusion only; no manuscript passage or transmission to later authors established.

sources.title: David Cusick, Sketches of Ancient History of the Six Nations, second edition (Tuscarora Village, 1828), Library of Congress facsimile.

verification.note: LOC catalogue metadata and downloaded facsimile checked. Read preface dated 10 June 1828 (PDF page 11) and opening of Part I (PDF pages 12–13). Cusick describes gathering materials and translating into English. The verified edition is 1828, not a claim to the first-ever Indigenous history or to a universal origin.

sources.title: William Apess, Eulogy on King Philip (1836), Voices of Democracy text and edition note.

verification.note: Read selected paragraphs 1–4, 10–21: Christian moral criticism, historical reinterpretation of colonial violence, and criticism of commemorating the Pilgrims. Textual authentication page distinguishes 1836/1837 editions and the 1992 O’Connell edition used online. Interpretation concerns Apess’s argument, not independent verification of every event he narrates.

sources.title: William W. Warren, History of the Ojibway People (first published 1885); Minnesota Historical Society second-edition description.

verification.note: Publisher description checked: first publication in 1885, accounts from relatives and tribal leaders, transcription for a nineteenth-century white readership, and acknowledged interpretive limitations. Book body and manuscript completion date not checked.

sources.title: Jenifer Curnow, Wiremu Maihi Te Rangikāheke, Dictionary of New Zealand Biography (1990), Te Ara.

verification.note: Read biography sections on manuscripts written before 1854, historical narration, genealogy, land, and Grey’s unacknowledged alterations and reuse in 1853–55 publications. Institutional biographical account, not a reading of the manuscripts; no direct influence on Smith or Walker established.

sources.title: Edward Ahenakew, Voices of the Plains Cree (1973), edited by Ruth M. Buck; 1995 University of Regina edition with Stan Cuthand’s introduction.

verification.note: Downloaded 1995 edition. Checked imprint and contents; read Cuthand’s introduction pp. xii–xiv and xx and Buck’s 1973 introduction pp. 1–2. Thunderchild’s 1923 narration, Ahenakew’s recording, Old Keyam’s literary form, and later editorial selection remain distinct. No full-book reading or claim that the printed stories are unmediated transcripts. Cuthand’s introductory recollections contain a chronological inconsistency about seeing Thunderchild; that detail is not adopted.

sources.title: Edward Ahenakew, Cree Trickster Tales, Journal of American Folklore 42, no. 166 (1929): 309–353.

verification.note: Publisher issue contents checked: author E. Ahenakew, October–December 1929, pages 309–353, DOI 10.2307/535231. Article body unread. Oral-tradition publication is not automatically classified as a modern historical-method manifesto.

sources.title: Bruce Biggs, Pei Te Hurinui Jones, Dictionary of New Zealand Biography (1998), Te Ara.

verification.note: Read biographical sections on recording Tainui genealogies, Māhinārangi (1929), English manuscript by about 1936, disputed reuse by Kelly in 1949, and posthumous Ngā iwi o Tainui (1995). Publication, composition and later editing distinguished. Original works unread; King Pōtatau’s genre is disputed in this account.

sources.title: M. P. K. Sorrenson, Peter Henry Buck (Te Rangi Hīroa), Dictionary of New Zealand Biography (1996, updated 2002), Te Ara.

verification.note: Read institutional biography including interwar research and Vikings of the Sunrise (1938). Adds a dated earlier contribution to the existing person and strand; survey body unread. Does not equate Buck’s ethnology with later decolonizing methodology.

sources.title: Métis Nation of Ontario, Métis Scholar Olive Dickason Passes (18 April 2011).

verification.note: Read MNO’s recognition of Dickason as Métis and original Cultural Commission member. Supports contextual affiliation and 1977 doctorate. The appended obituary’s single-founder claim and its inconsistent dating of Canada’s First Nations are not adopted.

sources.title: Olive Patricia Dickason, The Myth of the Savage and the Beginnings of French Colonialism in the Americas (1984); University of Alberta Press description of later edition.

verification.note: Publisher description checked for study of early contact and European representations. Page lists a 1997 edition; original 1984 date cross-checked with MNO account and contemporary bibliographic review. Body unread; publisher blurbs are not passage-level findings.

sources.title: Olive Patricia Dickason, Canada’s First Nations: A History of Founding Peoples from Earliest Times (McClelland & Stewart, 1992), Canadian Language Museum book record.

verification.note: Museum book record checked: original author, 1992 date, publisher and ISBN 0771028008, description of historical synthesis combining history, anthropology and archaeology. Not a reading of the survey or evidence of every later reception claim.

sources.title: Ron Laliberté, Howard Adams (1921–2001), Indigenous Saskatchewan Encyclopedia, University of Saskatchewan.

verification.note: Read institutional biography: doctorate in History of Education and Saskatchewan appointment in 1966, Prison of Grass (1975), Métis and Marxist contextual interpretation, and colonialism/assimilation critique. Book body unread. This distinguishes academic participation before 1970 from later expansion.

sources.title: Emma LaRocque, Defeathering the Indian (Book Society of Canada, 1975), Smithsonian Libraries catalogue.

verification.note: Indexed Smithsonian catalogue author/title/year checked; direct opening unavailable. Catalogue uses LaRoque spelling and identifies LaRocque in authority form. Bibliographic inclusion only.

sources.title: Emma LaRocque author profile, University of Manitoba Press.

verification.note: Publisher author description checked for Defeathering the Indian, Canadian historiography and Indigenous representations. No first-edition body reading or universal methodological claim.

sources.title: Yolande Ricard, Georges E. Sioui: interview, Québec français 80 (winter 1991): 76–78, discussing Pour une autohistoire amérindienne (1989).

verification.note: Read author’s explanation of autohistory on p. 77 and adjacent discussion. Title/metadata identifies original 1989 French work. Supports his proposal to bring Indigenous self-interpretation and transmitted traditions into historical discourse. Claims about all Amerindian values are attributed to Sioui, not adopted as a universal description.

sources.title: Georges E. Sioui, For an Amerindian Autohistory (1992), translated by Sheila Fischman, McGill-Queen’s University Press.

verification.note: Publisher description, translator, foreword credit and October 1992 date checked. French original 1989 separately evidenced by contemporary interview. Body unread; publisher’s claim that he was the first is not adopted.

sources.title: D’Arcy McNickle papers, Newberry Library archival finding aid.

verification.note: Indexed custodial finding-aid sections checked for They Came Here First (1949), University of Saskatchewan work and creating the Center for the History of the American Indian in 1972, named after him in 1984. Direct requests returned 403; evidence is limited to the indexed institutional account, not archival item or book reading.

sources.title: John Joseph Mathews, The Osages: Children of the Middle Waters (1961), University of Oklahoma Press later-edition description.

verification.note: Publisher description checked for oral history, recorded history and author’s community experience, and Wah’Kon-Tah’s original 1932 date. Page dates the paperback to 1981; original 1961 date cross-checked against Oklahoma Historical Society biography. Neither body read.

sources.title: John Joseph Mathews, Oklahoma Historical Society Encyclopedia.

verification.note: Institutional biographical account checked for Wah’Kon-Tah (1932) and The Osages (1961). Retain genre differences rather than treating the two as interchangeable methodological treatises.

sources.title: Lilikalā Kameʻeleihiwa, Native Land and Foreign Desires (1992), Bishop Museum Press description.

verification.note: Publisher description checked for Hawaiian-language sources, land relations and Māhele interpretation, and named nineteenth-century Hawaiian intellectuals Malo, ʻĪʻī and Kamakau. Original 1992 date checked against bibliographic record. Body and specific transmission passages unread.

sources.title: Haunani-Kay Trask, From a Native Daughter (1993; revised 1999), University of Hawaiʻi Press description.

verification.note: Publisher description explicitly distinguishes original 1993 publication and May 1999 revision and describes colonialism, sovereignty, racism and gender discrimination. Neither edition read in full; revision additions are not backdated to 1993.

sources.title: Kevin Gilbert, Living Black: Blacks Talk to Kevin Gilbert (1977), Victorian Government Library Service catalogue.

verification.note: Catalogue title, author, 1977 publication and interview/transcript description checked. Specific interviews, narrator credits and editorial methods remain unread; Gilbert is credited as compiler/interviewer, not sole producer of all knowledge.

sources.title: Ruby Langford Ginibi, Don’t Take Your Love to Town (Penguin, 1988), ANU Indigenous Australia work-based biographical record.

verification.note: Institutional record and its work-based descriptions checked: original 1988 edition, life narrative, localities and historical experiences. This is mediated biographical description, not full-book reading or a claim that autobiography and transmitted oral tradition are identical.

sources.title: Carlos Mamani Condori, Taraqu, 1866–1935: masacre, guerra y renovación en la biografía de Eduardo L. Nina Qhispi (La Paz: Ediciones Aruwiyiri, 1991), Library of Congress HLAS record.

verification.note: Indexed LOC bibliographic record and attributed HLAS annotation checked: author, 1991 imprint and local Aymara land/rights subject. Direct opening unavailable. Book body, oral-history method and institutional founding role not checked.

sources.title: Blair Stonechild and Bill Waiser, Loyal Till Death: Indians and the North-West Rebellion (Fifth House, 1997), bibliographic record.

verification.note: Original 1997 imprint, title and both author credits checked in publisher/catalogue metadata, corroborated by Waiser’s public CV. Book body unread. Bibliographic inclusion preserves outside coauthor credit and does not accept every interpretation of 1885.

sources.title: Emma LaRocque, Native Writers Resisting Colonizing Practices in Canadian Historiography and Literature (PhD dissertation, University of Manitoba, 1999), p. 34.

verification.note: Downloaded thesis; checked title/date and read p. 34. LaRocque relates her 1974 curriculum research to Defeathering the Indian and describes its pedagogical and resistance purposes. This is her 1999 retrospective account, not a full reading of the 1975 book or dissertation.
